_loc_provenance: LoC tokens (prod_loc, support_loc, iac_loc, system_model_loc, total_loc, support_ratio) are POINT-IN-TIME source-tree category counts measured 2026-08-03 on the system's repository (parent repo, HEAD ce0bde110fbb at measurement) via a categorized line-count tool. Category map: prod_loc=Production Code (491,090); support_loc=support-apparatus rollup (1,501,907 = tests + lints + load-bearing docs + agent infrastructure + tools; support_ratio 3.0 = support_loc/prod_loc); iac_loc=Infrastructure as Code (35,323); system_model_loc=System-model meta-files (28,507); total_loc=whole-tree code, raw (2,824,878; the tool also reports a semantic total of 2,083,089 that excludes snapshot/history docs — total_loc keeps the raw whole-tree definition the 2026-07-23 baseline used). NOTE on the iac/system-model jump vs the 2026-07-23 baseline (8,446 / 7,380): a category re-partition landed in the count tool late on 2026-07-23 (after the baseline run) that carved previously-UNCOUNTED deploy/** production source and top-level system-models/*.py modules into these two categories — the jump is a coverage fix in the tool, not organic growth. These are source-tree counts, NOT the 15.7M engineering-line churn figure from a repo-activity histogram over the git history (which measures added+deleted lines over time). D1/D2 RECONCILIATION (Part-5 assembly, 260806): prod_loc/support_loc are set to the delta-consistent 'now' snapshot (491,090 / 1,501,907) that reproduces the +45%/+21% support-ratio-curve growth deltas and equals the support-ratio table 'now — Aug 3' row; the earlier (higher) measurement is superseded and must not reappear. The EXACT canonical figure (choice of canonical SHA; design recommends 07af718a) is finalized at the read-only metrics-miner run and remains user-gated — these token values are the authoritative in-tree snapshot pending that confirmation.
_commit_provenance: Commit tokens (commits_total, commits_per_week, commits_per_day, peak_week_commits, study_weeks) from a repo-activity histogram over the git history (commits metric) on the parent repo, measured 2026-08-03 at HEAD ce0bde110fbb (20 full weeks, 2026-03-12 -> 2026-07-23 week-starts, i.e. through 2026-07-29). commits_total=23,215 over 20 weeks; sustained rate ~200 commits/day (~1,000-1,400/week; 20-week mean 1,161/week); peak_week_commits=3,329 (week of 2026-05-21). commits_per_day was corrected 500 -> 200 (500/day implied ~3,500/week, a rate only the single peak week approached).
_workweeks_note: Displayed rounded UP to a whole week for readability (the reader needn't do fractions): the underlying estimate is hours_per_course 300 / a 40-hour week = 7.5, presented as ~8.
_model_count_note: The Model Zoo census: 7 general model types (G1-G7) + 19 real typed system-models (M1-M19) + 3 split-out sub-models (M18a, M18b, M14a) = 29 named models. Presented as EVIDENCE for the 4+1 thesis (a zoo large enough that one view is never enough), not as a target to hit.
_mechanism_count_note: Tracks the companion catalogue census (the <!--census:controls--> macro / INDEX total). Word-form, kept approximate ('around ...') so small drift as new mechanisms land does not falsify the prose. Update when the census crosses a round number. Census at last sync: 83.
_missing_model_pilot_note: The Missing Model Metric pilot (the missing-model-metric pilot, Phase 1). Ran a code->model tracer over 144 tests in the dispatch/orchestration subsystem — deliberately the most heavily-modelled slice. missing_model_pilot_fraction=0.56: 56% of those tests exercise production code that traces to no invariant, state machine, or service edge. missing_model_pilot_test_count=144. The number is a LOWER bound (import-reach over-counts DETAILS_NODE). Sharpening finding: every orphan reached code anchored at the coarse Component level but with no fine behavioral model — a granularity gap. Surfaced three genuine candidate missing-models, down-weighted two missing-anchor clusters.

_support_ratio_curve_provenance: The figures the support-ratio-curve data-claims entry holds, tokenized for the same anchoring reason as control-growth: section 5.2 is that claim's source chapter, so a [data:] marker there would cross-ref itself. Source: the 29-week history-mining pass (acquired 260925.103236, series in data/factory-archaeology-260925/loc_weekly.csv), which carries its OWN category path-map. mined_support_ratio_plateau='3.5 and 3.9' is the mature-era band of the support_ratio_excl_docs column, which runs 3.46 (week 29) to 3.94 (week 22) across the plateau; it is stored as ONE token holding BOTH bounds so the band cannot drift half-updated. mined_test_loc='1.75 million' is test_loc at the final week (1,754,638). DO NOT RECONCILE mined_support_ratio_plateau AGAINST support_ratio=3.0 — they are different quantities from different instruments, and the gap is DISCLOSED in the chapter, not a defect: support_ratio=3.0 is the authored 2026-08-03 snapshot from the categorized line-count tool (support_loc/prod_loc), while the plateau band is the later mining pass's own re-derivation excluding documentation. Both measure 2026-08-03 among other weeks and disagree there (3.0 vs 3.94) because the category boundaries differ; the chapter overlays the two recoverable authored snapshots as diamonds so the definitional gap stays visible, and states that only the TREND is comparable across the two. Neither is the 'earlier (higher) measurement' the D1/D2 reconciliation in _loc_provenance supersedes — that one is a rival measurement of prod_loc/support_loc at the SAME 2026-08-03 snapshot by the SAME tool, which is a different thing entirely. RESIDUE, left as the author's prose rather than flattened: (a) the band's lower bound 3.5 is absent from the entry's holds[] list, so it is not governed on its own — it rides inside this one band token, and adding a bare '3.5' to the ledger would also make the leak lint fire on section locators like '§3.5'; (b) 5.2 and its figure caption both say the plateau settles 'around three-to-one' in word form, and word forms are not token-rendered, so a change to the band here must update them by hand.
